# Best open-ear earbuds for running

Prices come from the reviews and may have changed. I only have the article URLs from my search, so the links below go to the pages where each product's buy buttons appear.

## Top picks

| Need | Pick | Price | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Best overall clip-on | Bose Ultra Open Earbuds | $199 (list $299) | Best sound and comfort of the clip-ons. Runner's World named it best overall. WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run. |
| Best bone conduction | Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 | $125-$180 | Keeps your ears most open. It has 12 hours of battery and IP55 water resistance. |
| Best for long runs | Shokz OpenDots 2 | $200 | 10 hours per charge (40 with case) and IP57. WIRED's top overall pick. |
| Best value | Nothing Ear (Open) | $99 (list $149) | SoundGuys' pick for running. It has strong bass for this category and an IP54 rating. |
| Budget | JLab Flex Open | about $40-$50 | A low-risk way to see if clip-ons work for you. Sound is less detailed. |

## Details and caveats

- **Bose Ultra Open** has only IPX4 water resistance and about 7 hours of battery. Runner's World says to skip it if you run in heavy rain. It also says Bose plans to release a new open-ear pair within a month, so you may want to wait for that or for further discounts. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** sounds fuller than older bone-conduction models, but WIRED found it less clear than the Bose, especially for podcasts. The neckband can clash with ponytails and hoods. RTINGS says the Bose is slightly better for most people, but the Shokz is tougher and works better if you have ear piercings. WIRED's review is from 2024, so check current pricing. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)
- **Shokz OpenDots 2** is pricey, but it wraps the earlobe and leaves the top of your ear free for glasses and hats. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- **Nothing Ear (Open)** and the other SoundGuys picks are listed here: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2** is an ear-hook design with IP55 and 10 hours of battery. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon. Soundcore's own store lists it at $129.99, or about $104 with code AFSC20 (tested in the cart on 2026-10-22, expires 2026-12-31). The Amazon price looks better, so compare both. [Buy at Soundcore](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2) (affiliate link; the page says it pays the site a commission at no cost to you.) [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- **SoundPeats PearlClip Pro** is another $50 option, listed by WIRED. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

## My suggestion

- If sound quality matters most and you can spend about $200, get the Bose.
- If you want maximum awareness and a secure fit, get the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, especially at $125.
- If you want a good price, get the Nothing Ear (Open) at $99.

Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise, and none of them guarantees safety on the road, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

Do you use an iPhone or Android, and does your budget have a ceiling? I can narrow this down.
